note: Bored-investor critique applied. Uncovered 2 blockers regarding the warm terminal promise and Foreman-readiness of the UUID capture, plus two major telemetry gaps.

findings.criterion: clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal that narrates what was done
findings.message: The North Star explicitly mandates that 'clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal'. However, W6 introduces a '1-click/2-action path' where the first click only opens a static Layer-1 chrome view, requiring a second explicit 'Resume live' action to attach and swap in the actual live pane. This directly violates the 1-click warm terminal contract.

W4 states that engine_session_id capture will use either 'slug-dir watch... or PTY-banner parse per the W1 spike'. A Foreman-ready implementation plan must be completely deterministic; it cannot delegate architectural 'or' decisions to the build agent based on the outcome of an earlier wave's spike. This ambiguity blocks autonomous execution.

W4 mandates 'eager finalize on EVERY end path (kill, close/park...)'. When a ConPTY session is hard-killed, the underlying engine/sidecar may still be flushing the final tokens to disk. Eagerly reading the usage immediately on the kill path without a synchronization or flush-wait mechanism guarantees that the final turns of killed sessions will be silently undercounted, violating the 'not zero-by-omission' rule.

findings.criterion: Every Anchor session — interactive ConPTY or one-shot job — leaves an honest, machine-verified trail of what it cost
findings.message: W6 implements orientation as a 'read-only plan-mode one-shot job'. According to W4, one-shot jobs are routed into the usage ledger. If orientation is tracked as a standard one-shot job, clicking a tile multiple times will spawn multiple orientation jobs, inflating the project's total cost with read-only overhead. The plan must explicitly define how orientation job costs are classified or excluded from the primary effort rollup to avoid double-counting.
